s1.syndrome_frame: Acute vision loss with intraocular hemorrhage and crystalline deposits
salient_findings: Spontaneous hyphema and vitreous hemorrhage in one eye
Presence of glistening crystals in the anterior chamber
Morning glory optic disc anomaly with retinal detachment
key_facts: Hyphema and vitreous hemorrhage occurred spontaneously
Multiple glistening crystals were observed in the anterior chamber
Number of aqueous crystals increased as hyphema resolved
Iridescent, needle-like crystals were seen floating in the aqueous
Morning glory optic disc anomaly was present
Low-lying detachment of the peripapillary retina was observed
Chronic retinal detachment was found after vitreous hemorrhage resolution

shortlist.label: Bietti crystalline corneoretinal dystrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of iridescent, needle-like crystals in the aqueous humor

shortlist.label: Primary hyperoxaluria
shortlist.why_kept: Association with crystalline deposits in the eye

shortlist.label: Cystinosis
shortlist.why_kept: Crystalline deposits in the cornea and conjunctiva

shortlist.label: Morning glory syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of morning glory optic disc anomaly

shortlist.label: Crystalline retinopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Spontaneous hyphema and vitreous hemorrhage with crystalline deposits

raw.rationale: The presence of iridescent, needle-like crystals in the aqueous humor is characteristic of cystinosis, which is known to cause crystalline deposits in the eyes.

rejected.label: Bietti crystalline corneoretinal dystrophy
rejected.why: It typically presents with crystalline deposits in the retina, not in the aqueous humor.

rejected.label: Primary hyperoxaluria
rejected.why: It is associated with oxalate crystals in the urine and kidneys, not typically in the eyes.

rejected.label: Morning glory syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient has a morning glory optic disc anomaly, this condition does not typically cause crystalline deposits in the aqueous humor.

rejected.label: Crystalline retinopathy
rejected.why: This term is more general and does not specifically explain the presence of crystals in the aqueous humor as seen in cystinosis.

gold: Synchysis scintillans with morning glory disc anomaly and chronic retinal detachment
